title: Camel Tracks and Silk Rolls: The Trade Stories of the Silk Road
title_zh: 驼铃与丝绸卷：丝绸之路上的贸易故事
intro_zh: 本文约 532 词，讲述丝绸之路上的贸易故事：从长安出发的驼队、张骞的见闻、粟特商人的中转生意、罗马人对丝绸的痴迷，以及纸张与思想的西传。文章含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，配有中文翻译与 4 道阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: At dawn, a line of camels loaded with rolls of silk left the gates of Chang'an, the capital of Han China. The goods on their backs were worth more than a small town. This caravan was heading west, into deserts, mountains and more than twenty small kingdoms. No one in it knew exactly how far the journey would go.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明时分，一队驮着丝绸卷的骆驼离开汉朝都城长安的城门。它们背上的货物价值超过一座小镇。这支商队一路向西，穿过沙漠、群山和二十多个小国。商队中没有人确切知道这趟旅程会走多远。

paragraphs.en: The story usually begins with an official named Zhang Qian. In 138 BC the emperor sent him west to find allies against a northern enemy. He was captured, held for years, and came home with almost nothing — except detailed news of distant lands. He described cities with grapes, alfalfa and tall horses that sweated blood. That report changed what Chinese rulers wanted to buy.
paragraphs.zh: 这个故事通常从一位名叫张骞的官员讲起。公元前138年，皇帝派他西行，寻找对抗北方敌人的盟友。他遭到扣留，被囚禁多年，几乎空手而归——却带回了关于遥远国度的详细见闻。他描述了盛产葡萄、苜蓿和汗血高头大马的城市。这份报告改变了中国统治者想要购买的东西。

paragraphs.en: Trade grew slowly, then steadily. Silk went west. In return came horses from Central Asia, glass and wool from Persia, gold, silver and spices from India. Silk was so precious that Han soldiers were sometimes paid in it, and one fine roll could buy a horse or cover a family's taxes for a year. Because it was light, easy to fold and hard to fake, silk worked as money as well as cloth.
paragraphs.zh: 贸易起初发展缓慢，后来逐渐稳定增长。丝绸向西流去；作为回报，中亚的马匹、波斯的玻璃和羊毛、印度的黄金、白银和香料向东而来。丝绸极为珍贵，有时汉朝士兵的军饷就用丝绸支付，一匹上好的丝绸可以买一匹马，或者支付一个家庭一年的赋税。由于丝绸轻便、易折叠又难以仿造，它既是布料，也当货币使用。

paragraphs.en: Few traders walked the entire route. Most goods passed from hand to hand, and the real masters of the road were Sogdian merchants. These Central Asian traders spoke several languages, kept accounts in their own script, and ran family firms from Samarkand to the Chinese border. Their language became the common tongue of trade across the desert. Letters they left at Dunhuang complain about slow sales and unpaid debts.
paragraphs.zh: 很少有商人走完整条路线。大多数货物都是转手多次，而这条商路真正的主人是粟特商人。这些中亚商人会说多种语言，用自己的文字记账，经营着从撒马尔罕到中国边境的家族商号。他们的语言成为穿越沙漠的通用贸易语言。他们留在敦煌的信件里，抱怨货物滞销和欠款难收。

paragraphs.en: Far to the west, Rome fell in love with silk. Nobody there knew how it was made; some writers believed it grew on trees. The demand was huge. In the first century AD, the scholar Pliny the Elder grumbled that Rome was losing a fortune every year to buy a fabric so thin that a woman could hardly be said to be dressed in it. Each Roman paid the profits of a dozen middlemen.
paragraphs.zh: 在遥远的西方，罗马爱上了丝绸。那里没人知道丝绸是怎么造出来的，有些作家甚至以为它长在树上。需求十分巨大。公元一世纪，学者老普林尼抱怨说，罗马每年为了购买这种薄得几乎算不上衣服的布料而流失大量财富。每个罗马人都为十几个中间商的利润买单。

paragraphs.en: Yet silk was never the road's only luxury. Ideas travelled with the caravans. Buddhism reached China from India along these paths, and with it came new styles of painting and sculpture in the caves at Dunhuang. Paper, which Chinese craftsmen made from rags and bark, moved west and reached Baghdad by the eighth century. A road that began with cloth ended up carrying knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 然而丝绸从来不是这条路上唯一的奢侈品。思想也随商队一起旅行。佛教沿着这些道路从印度传入中国，随之而来的还有敦煌石窟中新的绘画与雕塑风格。中国工匠用破布和树皮制成的纸向西传播，到八世纪时已抵达巴格达。一条始于布料的道路，最终承载了知识。

paragraphs.en: Dunhuang, on the edge of the Gobi Desert, shows how mixed that world was. Travellers arriving there had to register at a checkpoint and pay a tax on their goods. Nearby, in a sealed cave, archaeologists later found tens of thousands of documents in Chinese, Tibetan, Sanskrit, Sogdian and other languages. They include contracts, receipts, prayers and letters home — everyday records of a busy, practical people.
paragraphs.zh: 位于戈壁沙漠边缘的敦煌，展现了那个世界有多么多元。到达那里的旅客必须在关卡登记，并为货物缴税。附近一个被封存的洞窟中，考古学家后来发现了数万份用汉语、藏语、梵语、粟特语等多种语言写成的文书。其中包括契约、收据、祷文和家书——一个忙碌而务实的民族的日常记录。

paragraphs.en: By the fifteenth century the overland traffic had almost stopped. Sea routes were cheaper and safer, and the empires along the way had grown unfriendly. But the exchange never really ended, and it shaped both sides for good. Chinese paper, Indian numbers and Persian designs are still part of daily life in Europe, while the old caravan towns are once again busy with trade.
paragraphs.zh: 到十五世纪，陆路交通几乎停止。海上路线更便宜也更安全，沿途的帝国也变得不再友善。但交流从未真正结束，而且它永久地塑造了双方。中国的纸、印度的数字和波斯的图案至今仍存在于欧洲人的日常生活中，而那些古老的商队城镇也再次因贸易而繁忙起来。

questions.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: The Silk Road was mainly a Chinese plan for selling silk abroad.
The Silk Road carried goods and ideas between East and West for many centuries.
Roman writers were wrong about how silk was produced.
Sea routes were so good that land trade was useless.
questions.explain: 全文从驼队出发写起，依次讲货物、商人、罗马的需求、思想的传播和敦煌文书，落脚于交流长期塑造了东西方，因此 B 最全面。A 把丝绸之路窄化为中国卖丝绸；C 只是第五段的一个细节；D 与原文不符，原文只说海路更便宜更安全。

questions.q: What did Zhang Qian bring back from his journey?
options: A large number of tall horses.
Rolls of silk and bags of gold.
questions.explain: 第二段明确说他 almost nothing — except detailed news of distant lands，即带回了远方国度的详细见闻。他没有带回盟友（任务失败），马匹和葡萄只是他描述的内容，不是他带回来的东西。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the letters the Sogdian merchants left at Dunhuang?
options: Trade did not always go smoothly for those who ran it.
Sogdian merchants wrote only in Chinese.
Most merchants travelled the whole route alone.
The desert road was closed for most of the year.
questions.explain: 第四段说信件里抱怨 slow sales and unpaid debts（滞销与欠款），可推知经商并非总能顺利获利。B 与原文所列多种语言矛盾；C 与 Few traders walked the entire route 相反；D 文中未提。

questions.q: The word "precious" in Paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 第三段用军饷以丝绸支付、一匹丝绸可买一匹马或抵一年赋税来说明丝绸 precious，可见其义为“值钱的、贵重的”，故选 B。A、D 描述的是轻便易带，属于原因而非词义；C 强调稀少，原文强调的是价值高。
